content.text: ## Root cause Liquid doesn't support running a filter (`| date: "%m"`) inside square-bracket hash lookup syntax. The template: ```liquid {{ site.data.de_months[page.date | date: "%m"] }} ``` is invalid Liquid — building confirmed it with a syntax warning (`Expected close_square but found pipe`) and silently rendered as empty. So **every** post's German date was missing its month name (e.g. `10. 2026`), not just September — you likely just noticed it on the new September posts first. ## Fix In both `_layouts/article.html` and `de/artikel/index.md`, computed the month key first with `{% assign %}`, then indexed into `de_months`: ```liquid {% assign de_month_key = page.date | date: "%m" %} {{ page.date | date: "%-d" }}. {{ site.data.de_months[de_month_key] }} {{ page.date | date: "%Y" }} ``` Verified with a local `bundle exec jekyll build`: no more Liquid warnings, and both the article page and `/de/artikel/` listing now render `10. For a small German museum with no tech staff, AI realistically delivers:

- 30–50% reduction in time spent on routine content drafting

- Reduction in low-value email and phone enquiries handled by staff

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Can a small museum use AI without any IT staff?**
Yes — content drafting with general-purpose AI, DeepL-based translation, and FAQ chatbots for logistics questions all work with no technical infrastructure, just a monthly subscription and a staff member to review outputs.

**What AI projects still require outside technical help?**
Two: cataloguing at scale (processing hundreds or thousands of records) and visitor-facing chatbots grounded in your own collection data. Both are one-time, fixed-scope builds rather than ongoing retainers.

A 30–50% reduction in time spent on routine content drafting, affordable translation into 2–3 additional languages, and fewer routine enquiries reaching staff — not a full transformation of the visitor experience overnight.

Whether the catalogue is digitised, whether a staff member will own and review the tool, and whether there's one specific, well-defined task the AI is meant to solve.
